verses.1: And these people who came to David to seek help were still in hiding, because they were under the protection of Saul, son of Kish. And they were among the powerful warriors who helped him in battle.
verses.2: The pillars of the temple are made of stones and bricks; they were constructed from copper by the sons of Shaul.
verses.3: Horeš, Ahijzer, and Yoash, sons of Shemaiah the Givet; Yiziel and Pelt, sons of Azmaveth. And they are blessed.
verses.4: And the high priest will hear from the thirty, and from those thirty.
verses.5: And Jeremiah, and Jachaziel, and Jonathan, and Yozabad the Gederati.
verses.6: Eluzai, Virimot, Baalya, Shmariahu, and Shpatiyahu, the wicked ones.
verses.7: Elkanah, Ishiyahu, Azarael, Yo’ezer, and Yashavam the Karchim.
verses.8: And Joela and Zvadia, sons of Yeroham, from the tribe of Gad.
verses.9: And from those who were chosen, they were divided among David’s troops. They were soldiers who fought in battles: men who could throw stones and spears, and those with lion-like faces. They served as soldiers on the mountains, ready to fight.
verses.10: The first helper was Eliyahu the second, and the third was Eliezer.
verses.11: From the fourth place comes Jeremiah the fifth.
verses.12: At this time, Eliel the Seventeenth shall reign.
verses.13: John the Eighth, Elzabad the Seventeenth.
verses.14: Jeremiah the rich man, from the tribe of Manasseh, had twelve sons.
verses.15: These are the sons of Gad. The leaders of the tribe were one hundred in number, including both the small and the large ones.
verses.16: These are those who crossed the Jordan in the first month. They filled all their containers with water, and they drove away all the enemies to the east and to the west.
verses.17: And they came from the sons of Benjamin and Judah, all the way to Bethlehem, to David.
verses.18: David went out before them, stood up, and said to them, “If you come to me for help, then I will be willing to help you. But if you come to deceive me and make me suffer without any reason, then we will see whether our ancestors’ gods will help us or not.”
verses.19: And the Spirit of God anointed David and his people, the sons of Jesse, with peace. Peace for you, and peace for your helpers, because your helpers are God. David accepted them as kings over their tribes.
verses.20: And from Manasseh, they fell upon David when he went out with the Philistines to fight against Saul. They did not help him, because in their own plans, the Philistines sent them to say, “Our lord will fall at Saul’s hands.”
verses.21: As he walked towards Ziklag, they fell upon him from Manasseh, Adnah, Yozabad, Vidiael, Michael, Yozabad, Elihuah, and Zeltai, the leaders of the tribes that belonged to Manasseh.
verses.22: And they helped David against the enemies of David. All the leaders of the Philistines became his servants.
verses.23: For in that day, when they come to David for help, there will be a great camp like the camp of God.
verses.24: And these men from the tribes of Rephah and Zebulun came to David, their leader, asking him to take over Saul’s kingdom instead of him, as Jehovah had commanded.
verses.25: The sons of Judah carried away six thousand men and women. Their number was equivalent to the number of eyes on the bodies of the animals.
verses.26: From the sons of Shimeon, there were nobles from Chayil, who made up a group of seven thousand men.
verses.27: Of the sons of Levi, four thousand and six hundred.
verses.28: And the judge knew that Aaron and his men numbered three thousand and seventy.
verses.29: And Zadok was a young man, but he was very powerful. In his father’s house, there were forty-two people who served him.
verses.30: And from the sons of Benjamin, the brothers of Shaul, there were three thousand. And beyond that, their number increased, as they guarded the house of Shaul.
verses.31: And from the sons of Ephraim, there were forty thousand. Their names were recorded among the leaders of the tribes. They belonged to the house of their ancestors.
verses.32: And from half of Manasseh’s territory, twelve thousand men were chosen to come and rule over David.
verses.33: And the descendants of Issachar, those who understand discernment, shall know what will happen to Israel. Their leaders and all their relatives will be punished accordingly.
verses.34: From Mizbulun come the warriors who engage in warfare in all kinds of battles. There are fifty thousand warriors, and they act without any sense or compassion.
verses.35: And from my wings, I flew away with a thousand birds. With them were also thirty-seven elephants.
verses.36: And from the Danites, there were forty thousand soldiers; their number was one hundred and sixty thousand.
verses.37: And from those who go out to war, four hundred thousand will die in battle.
verses.38: And from Raubeni and Haggadi, and half of Manasseh’s territory, there were one hundred and ten thousand soldiers who served in all the armies for war.
verses.39: All these men of war, who were full of pride and arrogance, came together to rule David over all Israel. They also wanted to rule David alone as king over all Israel.
verses.40: And there were there with David six days during which they ate and drank, just as their ancestors had prepared for them.
verses.41: And also, those who work in the fields bring bread to those who are hungry and need food. They bring bread in baskets, on banners, and in various ways. In the morning, they eat coarse food, and they drink water and wine. And in the morning, they have plenty of sheep, for joy fills Israel.
